**4B.1 Research Note**

Bottom line: I found no credible 2024 evidence that Hasina genuinely accepted contestable power through free, fair, meaningful elections. The public record points the other way: boycotted/contested elections, widespread legitimacy doubts, repression of criticism, and coercive domestic control around the July crisis.

- [Fear of violence looms over a contentious Bangladesh election as polls open](https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/ap-top-news/2024/01/06/fear-of-violence-looms-over-a-contentious-bangladesh-election-as-polls-open/) — Associated Press, January 6-7, 2024. Claim: AP reported Hasina’s Awami League won a strong majority while the main opposition boycotted the vote, turnout was about 40%, and legitimacy doubts were widespread; this is direct evidence against meaningful electoral contestability. IDs: `4B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.10`
- [The US and UK say Bangladesh's elections extending Hasina's rule were not credible](https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/ap-top-news/2024/01/09/the-us-and-uk-say-bangladeshs-elections-extending-hasinas-rule-were-not-credible) — Associated Press, January 8, 2024. Claim: AP reported that key foreign partners viewed the election as not credible, reinforcing that Hasina did not leave power contestable through a fair electoral process. IDs: `4B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.10`
- [Bangladesh repression, security force abuses discredit elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024. Claim: HRW reported arrests for criticism and widespread repression before the January election, showing that dissent and competition were being chilled rather than allowed to determine power. IDs: `4B.1`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`
- [Bangladesh’s crackdown on protesters left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Claim: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity; that is consistent with a ruler relying on coercion rather than accepting contestable power. IDs: `4B.1`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024. Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence; this looks like coercive blame-shifting rather than acceptance of electoral contestability. IDs: `4B.1`, `3B.3`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `2B.6`
- [Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024. Claim: Reuters described internet/text shutdowns, curfew, and army deployment as the government escalated against protesters, which is incompatible with genuine acceptance that power should be contestable through meaningful elections. IDs: `4B.1`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `2B.4`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Hasina accepted free and fair elections as a genuine route to losing power.
- I also did not find strong counterevidence showing she voluntarily constrained herself to truly competitive electoral rules in practice.
- The best-supported conclusion is that elections were held, but not on terms that made power meaningfully contestable.
